title: As after summoning the Marahatta reinforcements to his support,

blocks.text: As after summoning the Marahatta reinforcements to his support, The latter, seeking the support of Ahmad Shah Abdali from Kabul, He called for the Pathan reinforcements to his support. (9) Thereafter, as he had called for Ahmad Shah's support, But he also got Delhi vacated from Marhatta occupation. (10) He laid a siege around Najibu Khan Ruhela's forces for the second time.
Who came rushing from Kabul (to crush the Marhattas). (11) Mir Mannu, having become lax after this development, As he received no support from Delhi (against Abdali).

Dewan Kaura Mal fortified his defences at Lahore (to combat the invaders). (12) Thereafter, the Dewan sent a very warm invitation to the Singhs, That the Hindus and the Singhs were fraternal followers of the same Guru.

Asking for the Singhs support on the basis of ideological affinity, He pleaded before the Singhs to push back Abdali's troops. (13) Offering not only to provide the Singhs with arms and ammunition, He was even prepared to offer a financial ransom to the Singhs.

Procuring a written assurance from Mir Mannu in favour of the Khalsa, He sent that written despatch to the Khalsa Panth. (14) (Mir Mannu) assured the Khalsa to start a dialogue with them, Soon after they had (jointly) repulsed the (Afghan) invader.

He would allow the Singhs to occupy that (Punjab) region, Which had always remained defiant to the Mughal rule. (15) (He narrated) that ever since Banda Bahadur's occupation of the hilly region, The Mughal empire had received no revenues from there.

As these hill chiefs had harassed the Khalsa Panth in the recent past, The Khalsa Panth should occupy the entire hill territory. (16) They must settle scores with the hill chiefs in the whole Doon valley.
They must collect as much revenue from the hills, As they collected from the Punjab region of their own. (17)
